cleanIntro: The Endura is a bolt-action inline whose breech plug comes out through the BACK of the receiver with a wrench, not off the muzzle end and not by hand. Everything below is CVA's own published procedure for this rifle and no other — the manual states on its cover page that its load data was tested for the Endura alone.

steps.title: Check the serial number against CVA's recall
steps.action: Before anything else, read the serial number off your rifle and check how it ends. CVA recalled a range of older in-line rifles by serial number, and no catalog listing can tell you whether yours is one of them — only the number stamped on your gun can.
steps.prose: This is the one check a guide cannot make for you. If the number ends in -95 or -96, stop here and call CVA; do not clean, load or fire the rifle.
steps.quote: Example of a recalled serial number: 61-13-XXXXXX-95 If you, or someone you know, have a CVA in-line with such a serial number, do not use or allow anyone else to use the rifle under any circumstances.
steps.cite: CVA® ENDURA™ OWNER'S MANUAL — ENDURA-MAN 07/25 — 22. Voluntary Recall, p.22
steps.warn: A recalled serial number means the rifle is not to be used at all — not by you and not by anyone you lend it to.

steps.title: Confirm the rifle is unloaded and unprimed
steps.action: Point the muzzle somewhere safe, rotate the safety lever rearward, then confirm two separate things: that no primer is sitting in the breech plug, and that there is no powder and no bullet in the barrel. A muzzleloader can be unprimed and still fully charged.
steps.prose: The primer and the charge are independent. Clearing one tells you nothing about the other, which is why the manual asks you to check both before a cleaning session begins.
steps.caution: Do this before the rifle goes in the vehicle, not after you get home.
steps.quote: ALWAYS make sure that your ENDURA is unloaded before leaving the range or the field. NEVER transport a loaded rifle in your vehicle or take a loaded rifle into the home. Before beginning your cleaning process, check again to be certain that the primer is out of the breech plug and there is no load in the barrel.
steps.cite: CVA® ENDURA™ OWNER'S MANUAL — ENDURA-MAN 07/25 — 19. Cleaning and Maintaining the Endura, p.18

steps.title: Unload a charged rifle from the breech
steps.action: If the rifle is still charged, unload it before stripping. Safety rearward, open the bolt and pull the primer, then press the bolt release on the left of the receiver and draw the bolt out. Unscrew the breech plug with the supplied wrench and push the bullet and powder out through the breech with the range rod.
steps.prose: The charge leaves through the back of the barrel, not the muzzle — that is the point of taking the plug out first. Pushing a seated bullet toward the muzzle against a closed breech is how a rod gets stuck.
steps.quote: To unload the loaded muzzleloader, follow these steps: 1. Rotate the safety lever rearward to the safe position. 2. Open the bolt and remove the primer from the breech plug. 3. Press the bolt release on the left side of the receiver and pull the bolt to the rear, removing it from the receiver.
steps.cite: CVA® ENDURA™ OWNER'S MANUAL — ENDURA-MAN 07/25 — 18. Unloading the Endura, p.17

steps.title: Take the bolt out of the receiver
steps.action: Safety rearward. Open the bolt and run it fully back, then press the bolt stop on the left side of the receiver and draw the bolt clear. Set it aside where it will not roll into grit.
steps.prose: The bolt stop is on the left flank of the receiver and has to be held in while the bolt clears it — the bolt will not simply pull out against it.
steps.quote: 1. Rotate the safety lever rearward to the safe position. 2. Open the bolt and move it to the rear. 3. Press the bolt stop, located on the left side of the receiver, and pull the bolt out of the receiver. Set aside.
steps.cite: CVA® ENDURA™ OWNER'S MANUAL — ENDURA-MAN 07/25 — 19. Cleaning and Maintaining the Endura, steps 1-3, p.18

steps.title: Prove the bore is empty with the range rod
steps.action: With the jag fitted, run the range rod down the muzzle until it stops. You are listening for a metallic clink as the jag meets the face of the breech plug, and measuring how much rod is left standing out of the muzzle — about 4½ inches on an empty barrel.
steps.prose: This is a measurement, not an impression. A dull stop instead of a clink, or noticeably more than 4½ inches of rod proud of the muzzle, means something is still down there.
steps.caution: If the rod stands out further than it should, there is a load or an obstruction in the bore. Clear it before going any further.
steps.quote: Make sure that the barrel is empty by inserting the Range Rod with the jag installed into the muzzle and down the bore. There should be a metallic “clink” as the jag makes direct contact with the face of the breech plug. The Range Rod (with the supplied Cleaning Jag installed) should extend from the muzzle about 4 ½ inches. If the Range Rod extends more than 4 ½ inches beyond the muzzle there is a load or some kind of obstruction in the bore. If so, it should be carefully removed before proceeding.
steps.cite: CVA® ENDURA™ OWNER'S MANUAL — ENDURA-MAN 07/25 — 19. Cleaning and Maintaining the Endura, step 5, p.18

steps.title: Remove the breech plug through the rear of the receiver
steps.action: Pass the breech plug wrench in through the back of the receiver and engage the hex on the plug. Put the short metal handle through the cross-hole at the rear of the wrench and turn counterclockwise to back the plug out.
steps.prose: The wrench reaches the plug from behind, down the bolt raceway — this is a bolt gun, so there is no getting at the plug from outside the barrel. A 7/16 socket on an extension does the same job if the supplied wrench has gone missing.
steps.quote: Insert the Breech Plug Wrench through the rear of the receiver and engage the hex shaped end of the breech plug. The wrench is supplied with a short metal handle. Insert the handle through the cross-hole at the rear of the wrench and turn counterclockwise to remove the breech plug. Note: A 7/16ths socket wrench with extension can be used instead of the supplied Breech Plug Wrench.
steps.cite: CVA® ENDURA™ OWNER'S MANUAL — ENDURA-MAN 07/25 — 19. Cleaning and Maintaining the Endura, step 6, p.18

steps.title: Scrub the bore with solvent
steps.action: Wet a patch with a copper-dissolving solvent, put it on the jag and push it through the bore with short scrubbing strokes until it comes out the far end. Repeat several times.
steps.prose: Short strokes rather than one long push — the scrubbing is what lifts fouling, and a single pass mostly just relocates it.
steps.quote: Wet a patch with a copper dissolving cleaning solvent and place it over the end of the cleaning jag. Push the patch through the bore using short scrubbing strokes until it exits the other end. Repeat this several times.
steps.cite: CVA® ENDURA™ OWNER'S MANUAL — ENDURA-MAN 07/25 — 19. Cleaning and Maintaining the Endura, step 8, p.18

steps.title: Oil the bore once it runs clean
steps.action: When dry patches are coming out relatively clean, finish with one patch carrying a small amount of oil.
steps.prose: The Endura's barrel is nitride-treated stainless and resists corrosion well, but the treatment is not a substitute for the oiled patch — long neglect will still let corrosion start.
steps.aside: If patches stop coming out clean, or start dragging, the manual sends you back to a bronze brush before you oil.
steps.quote: When clean, run a patch with a small amount of oil through the barrel.
steps.cite: CVA® ENDURA™ OWNER'S MANUAL — ENDURA-MAN 07/25 — 19. Cleaning and Maintaining the Endura, step 11, p.19

steps.title: Clean the breech plug and clear its flash hole
steps.action: Work the plug over with a rag and cotton swabs, concentrating on the primer pocket and the recess in the plug's front face. Then hold it up to a light and look straight through the flash hole — you should see daylight.
steps.prose: The flash hole is the smallest passage in the rifle and the first thing to block. A plugged one gives you a fired primer and an unfired charge, which leaves you standing at the bench with a loaded gun.
steps.caution: If the hole is not clear, pass a small wire through it before reinstalling.
steps.quote: Using a paper towel or rag and cotton swabs, thoroughly clean the breech plug paying special attention to the primer pocket and the recess in the front of the plug. Hold the breech plug towards a light and be certain that the flash hole in the center of the plug is clear.
steps.cite: CVA® ENDURA™ OWNER'S MANUAL — ENDURA-MAN 07/25 — 19. Cleaning and Maintaining the Endura, step 12, p.19

steps.title: Grease the plug threads and reinstall
steps.action: Coat the breech plug threads with breech plug grease or anti-seize, thread the plug back into the rear of the barrel and snug it with light pressure only.
steps.prose: Light pressure is the instruction, not a suggestion to be careful. Muzzleloader plugs seize when they are cranked down hard and left through a season of fouling; the anti-seize is what makes the next removal possible.
steps.quote: Coat the breech plug threads with breech plug grease or anti-seize and reinstall into the rear of the barrel. Tighten with light pressure only.
steps.cite: CVA® ENDURA™ OWNER'S MANUAL — ENDURA-MAN 07/25 — 19. Cleaning and Maintaining the Endura, step 13, p.19

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Bolt out, breech plug out, bore scrubbed and oiled, plug greased and back in. That is as far as CVA's routine cleaning goes for the Endura. Reinstall the bolt and function-check before the rifle goes away.
steps.prose: If you also took the stock off during cleaning, the retaining screws go back to 50 to 55 inch-pounds.
steps.quote: If you have removed the stock while cleaning your rifle, tighten the retaining screws to 50 – 55-inch pounds of torque during reassembly.
steps.cite: CVA® ENDURA™ OWNER'S MANUAL — ENDURA-MAN 07/25 — 19. Cleaning and Maintaining the Endura, step 18, p.20

deepSteps.title: Decide whether the bolt needs opening at all
deepSteps.action: Most of the time the bolt only wants an oily swab across the bolt face. Open it up only when a thorough cleaning is genuinely called for.
deepSteps.prose: CVA's own framing is that bolt disassembly is occasional, not routine. There is no fouling path into a closed Endura bolt the way there is on a rifle that blows back through an open breech.
deepSteps.quote: Usually, the bolt only requires light cleaning in the bolt face with an oily swab. Occasionally you may want to disassemble the bolt for thorough cleaning. To do so, grasp the bolt shroud in one hand, the bolt body in the other and twist the shroud clockwise approximately ¼ turn. The bolt shroud, with the attached firing pin assembly, will “pop” out of the bolt body.
deepSteps.cite: CVA® ENDURA™ OWNER'S MANUAL — ENDURA-MAN 07/25 — 19. Cleaning and Maintaining the Endura, p.19

deepSteps.title: Twist the shroud out of the bolt body
deepSteps.action: Hold the bolt shroud in one hand and the bolt body in the other, and twist the shroud clockwise about a quarter turn. The shroud comes out carrying the firing pin assembly with it, under spring pressure — expect it to pop rather than slide.
deepSteps.prose: A quarter turn, clockwise, and it releases. Keep a hand over it as it comes: the firing pin spring is compressed behind that shroud.
deepSteps.caution: The shroud and firing pin assembly leave the bolt body as one spring-loaded unit. Do not do this over a carpet.
deepSteps.quote: grasp the bolt shroud in one hand, the bolt body in the other and twist the shroud clockwise approximately ¼ turn
deepSteps.cite: CVA® ENDURA™ OWNER'S MANUAL — ENDURA-MAN 07/25 — 19. Cleaning and Maintaining the Endura, p.19

deepSteps.title: Unscrew the breech face from the bolt body
deepSteps.action: With a 9/16 inch or 14 mm wrench, or a crescent wrench, unscrew the breech face from the front of the bolt body.
deepSteps.prose: This is the face that carries the primer, so it is the part that actually sees combustion residue — it is the reason for opening the bolt in the first place.
deepSteps.quote: Using a 9/16 inch or a 14mm wrench, or a crescent wrench, unscrew the breech face from the bolt body.
deepSteps.cite: CVA® ENDURA™ OWNER'S MANUAL — ENDURA-MAN 07/25 — 19. Cleaning and Maintaining the Endura, step 14, p.19

deepSteps.title: Lubricate, reassemble the bolt and function-check
deepSteps.action: Lubricate the points the manual marks on its diagram, reassemble the bolt in reverse order, then put the bolt back in the receiver, close it, and check the trigger and safety before the rifle is stored.
deepSteps.prose: Going back together, the small tab on the shroud lines up with the matching groove in the bolt body, and the shroud is pressed in against the firing pin spring until the pin clicks into its detent. The function check is the last thing between an opened bolt and a loaded rifle.
deepSteps.caution: If anything in the trigger or safety does not behave as it should, this is a call to CVA, not something to adjust yourself.
deepSteps.quote: Insert the bolt into the receiver, close the bolt, and check the function of the trigger and safety. If you detect anything that is not as it should be, contact CVA customer Service immediately.
deepSteps.cite: CVA® ENDURA™ OWNER'S MANUAL — ENDURA-MAN 07/25 — 19. Cleaning and Maintaining the Endura, step 19, p.20

cleaning.name: Bore and breech plug
tasks: Solvent patch on the jag, short scrubbing strokes, repeat several times
Dry patches until they come out relatively clean
Bronze brush if the patches stay dirty or drag, then repeat
One lightly oiled patch to finish
Swab the plug's primer pocket and front recess; hold it to a light and confirm the flash hole is clear
Anti-seize on the plug threads, reinstall with light pressure only

cleaning.name: Bolt
tasks: Oily swab across the bolt face
Open the bolt only when a thorough clean is called for
Lubricate at the points marked in the manual's diagram

cleaning.name: Exterior
tasks: Wipe all exterior metal with an oily rag
If the stock came off, torque the retaining screws to 50-55 inch-pounds on reassembly

reassembly: Grease the breech plug threads and thread the plug into the rear of the barrel, light pressure only.

If the bolt was opened, reassemble it in reverse order — align the small tab on the shroud with the groove in the bolt body, press in against the firing pin spring until the pin clicks into its detent.
If the stock was removed, tighten the retaining screws to 50-55 inch-pounds.
Insert the bolt into the receiver and close it.
Check the trigger and safety before the rifle is stored or loaded.
fncheck: Insert the bolt into the receiver, close the bolt, and check the function of the trigger and safety. If anything is not as it should be, contact CVA Customer Service rather than firing the rifle.
